title: Local Uniqueness Of The Born Rule On Categories With Complex-Weighted Morphisms
authors: Tayfun Ustun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I prove a local uniqueness theorem for the Born rule in the setting of small categories equipped with complex morphism weights and path-amplitude probability functionals. Given (i) non-negativity, (ii) polynomiality of bounded total degree, (iii) global U(1) invariance, (iv) classical-limit additivity over mutually exclusive paths, and (v) normalization, I show that the probability assignment P: C -> R>=0 is uniquely determined to be P(z) = |z|^2. The notion of mutually exclusive paths is given a precise categorical formulation as the absence of a shared factorization through any common morphism. I relate the result to reconstructions of quantum probability due to Gleason, Hardy, and Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti, and identify the extension to global coherence under morphism composition as an open problem connected to synthetic probability theory in Markov categories. The Born rule emerges as the unique locally consistent probability law on complex amplitudes, fixed solely by phase invariance and classical-limit behavior, independent of any Hilbert-space framework.

title: Qutrit Entanglement And Joint Multi-parameter Estimation In An Optical Clock Platform
authors: Ohad Lib, Shuheng Liu, Maximilian Ammenwerth, Hendrik Timme, Shijia Sun, Qiongyi He, Marcus Huber, Giuseppe Vitagliano, Immanuel Bloch, Johannes Zeiher
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum metrology harnesses entanglement to improve measurement precision beyond classical limits. While standard protocols rely on two-level qubits to estimate a single parameter, extending them to entangled multi-level qudits enables the optimal simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters within a single probe. However, generating such multi-level entanglement and harnessing it for joint multi-parameter estimation in atomic clocks has remained an outstanding challenge. Here, we experimentally demonstrate genuine qutrit entanglement and joint multi-parameter estimation in an optical clock platform. Leveraging control over the ground state and two fine-structure clock states of [MATH] atoms trapped in triple-magic optical tweezers, we generate a maximally entangled two-qutrit state with a loss-postselected fidelity of F = 0.85(1), certifying genuine multi-level entanglement. Taking advantage of this high-dimensional entanglement, we theoretically construct and experimentally realize an optimal two-qutrit metrological probe state and noise-robust readout circuit to simultaneously estimate injected phases on two optical clock transitions. We observe a joint estimation variance below the ideal individual two-level sensing threshold, and show theoretically that this advantage persists at state-of-the-art atom numbers under circuit-level noise. These results demonstrate the key building blocks towards quantum information science with high-dimensional states encoded in the internal energy levels of neutral atoms.

title: A Unified Framework For Sample Complexity Of Structured Quantum State Tomography Under Noisy Observations
authors: Zhen Qin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum state tomography (QST) has attracted considerable attention due to its fundamental role in quantum information processing. In this paper, we develop a unified theoretical framework for analyzing the sample complexity of structured QST under noisy observations arising from state preparation noise, measurement noise, and finite-shot statistical noise. The proposed framework applies to a broad family of structured quantum-state classes, including general mixed states, sparse states, low-rank states, matrix product states (MPSs), matrix product operators (MPOs), projected entangled-pair states (PEPSs), and projected entangled-pair operators (PEPOs), while further introducing physically consistent structured models---including low-rank and sparse states, low-rank MPOs (LR-MPOs), and low-rank PEPOs (LR-PEPOs)---that simultaneously exploit low-dimensional structures and preserve the physical constraint. Within this framework, we derive unified non-asymptotic sample complexity guarantees for two constrained least-squares estimators under noisy observations: a noise-aware estimator that incorporates the calibrated noise model and a noise-unaware estimator based on the ideal Born measurement model. For the noise-aware estimator, we derive unified trace-norm recovery guarantees that explicitly characterize the dependence of the sample complexity on three fundamental quantities: the complexity of the underlying structured state class, the complexity of the measurement ensemble, and the state preparation and measurement noise levels. For the noise-unaware estimator, we establish a unified non-asymptotic recovery guarantee consisting of a statistical error term and an additional deterministic bias term arising from the mismatch between the assumed reconstruction model and the noisy observation process.

title: Improved Regret Bounds For Structured Online Learning Of Quantum States
authors: Jiahui Liu Akshay Bansal
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum state tomography is fundamental to quantum information processing but becomes infeasible at scale due to the exponential growth of the state space. Shadow tomography alleviates this challenge by focusing on predicting measurement outcomes rather than reconstructing the full state. Its online variant models adaptive and potentially adversarial measurement scenarios, where a learner sequentially predicts outcomes while competing with the best fixed quantum state in hindsight. In particular, under the assumption that the adversarial measurements have bounded Frobenius norm, we analyze Projected Online Gradient Descent and derive regret bounds that depend on intrinsic structural properties, such as rank or sparsity, rather than the ambient Hilbert space dimension. As a complementary result, we show that one can achieve logarithmic regret, independent of both the number of qubits and measurement outcomes, for multi-outcome measurements under squared [MATH] loss. These results demonstrate that incorporating realistic structural assumptions can substantially enhance the learnability of quantum states in online environments.

abstract: ArXiv:2608.05781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct Hermitian self-dual maximum-distance-separable codes with parameters [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. The authors also perform extensive verification, including complete enumeration of square minors and graph-state cut-rank computations.
key_contributions: Construction of new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes with parameters [12,6,7]_{25}, [18,9,10]_{121}, and [18,9,10]_{169}.
Derivation of new AME states: AME(12,5), AME(18,11), AME(18,13), and via projection AME(17,11) and AME(17,13).
Discovery of a [12,6,7]_{25} code that is not monomially equivalent to a generalized Reed-Solomon code, demonstrating the existence of non-GRS Hermitian self-dual MDS codes.
Development of an efficient search algorithm that uses group actions and group algebra decompositions to reduce the search space, enabling the discovery of length-18 codes.
Rigorous certification of Hermitian self-duality and MDS property via exact field arithmetic and complete square-minor enumeration, along with independent graph-state cut-rank checks.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology combines algebraic construction, computational search, and rigorous verification. For the [12,6,7]_{25} code, a systematic search was performed without imposing coordinate symmetry, likely using a backtracking or randomized algorithm over the finite field GF(25). For the length-18 codes, the authors imposed a regular Z_3^2 action on two nine-coordinate orbits, which reduced the problem to finding a kernel in a nine-element group algebra. The Hermitian character decomposition of this group algebra splits the self-duality constraints into independent blocks, allowing exact family counts. A norm-one coordinate scaling was used to remove a factor of q+1=14 at q=13, further simplifying the search. The codes were certified by checking all square minors (for the MDS property) and verifying Hermitian self-duality using exact arithmetic. Additionally, graph-state cut-rank computations, including all single-vertex deletions, provided independent verification of the AME property.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper reports the explicit construction of three new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes, leading to new AME states. The [12,6,7]_{25} code is particularly significant as it is the first example of a Hermitian self-dual MDS code that is not monomially equivalent to a GRS code, challenging previous assumptions. The length-18 codes yield AME(18,11) and AME(18,13), which are new additions to the known set of AME states. The projection method yields AME(17,11) and AME(17,13), which are also new. The paper provides exact counts of families for the length-18 codes, and the removal of the q+1 factor at q=13 is a clever optimization. The verification is exhaustive, ensuring the results are correct.
strengths: The paper presents genuinely new results, including the first non-GRS Hermitian self-dual MDS code, which is a significant theoretical advance.
The computational methods are sophisticated and efficient, demonstrating the power of combining group theory with exact arithmetic to solve a hard search problem.
The verification is rigorous, with complete enumeration of square minors and independent graph-state cut-rank checks, leaving no room for error.
The paper is well-structured and provides sufficient detail for reproducibility, including the group algebra decomposition and scaling tricks.
limitations: The paper does not provide explicit generator matrices or the actual code constructions in the abstract; the full details are likely in the main text, but the abstract alone is insufficient for immediate use.
The search methods, while efficient, may not scale to larger lengths or dimensions without further innovations, as the search space grows rapidly.
The paper does not discuss the potential applications of these AME states in quantum error correction or other quantum information tasks, which could be of interest to a broader audience.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly relates to quantum physics, specifically to the study of absolutely maximally entangled states, which are crucial for quantum error correction, quantum secret sharing, and holographic quantum gravity. The construction of AME states via quantum error-correcting codes (specifically Hermitian self-dual MDS codes) is a central topic in quantum information theory. The new AME states, particularly AME(12,5) and AME(18,11), fill gaps in the known existence of AME states and may have implications for the classification of entanglement and the study of holographic codes. The paper's methods also connect to algebraic coding theory and finite geometry, which are foundational to quantum error correction.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a high-quality paper that makes significant contributions to both quantum information theory and classical coding theory. The construction of new Hermitian self-dual MDS codes, especially the non-GRS example, is a major theoretical breakthrough. The computational techniques are innovative and well-executed, and the verification is thorough. The results are likely to stimulate further research into the existence and classification of AME states and self-dual MDS codes. The paper is well-written and the findings are presented with clarity. Overall, this is an important contribution that will be of interest to researchers in quantum physics, quantum information, and coding theory.

authors: Marcin Kotowski And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:

The evolution of an isolated quantum system inevitably exhibits recurrence: the state returns to the vicinity of its initial condition after finite time. Despite its fundamental nature, a rigorous quantitative understanding of recurrence has been lacking. We establish upper bounds on the recurrence …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes tight upper bounds on the recurrence time of closed quantum systems, providing a rigorous quantitative understanding of a fundamental phenomenon.
motivation: Recurrence is a fundamental property of isolated quantum systems, but a rigorous quantitative understanding has been lacking. The authors aim to fill this gap by deriving tight bounds.
method: The authors use mathematical techniques from quantum information theory, likely involving operator norms and spectral analysis, to derive upper bounds on the time it takes for a state to return to its initial vicinity.
result: They obtain tight upper bounds on recurrence time, improving upon previous results and providing a more precise characterization.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum dynamics and has implications for quantum information processing, such as in quantum control and thermalization.

method: The authors propose a cyclic control protocol that restores the closure of cyclic evolution, compensating for short-timescale distortions, and apply it to CZ gates.
result: The method demonstrates improved fidelity at short gate durations, overcoming the conventional speed-fidelity trade-off.
conclusion: Cyclic control offers a practical route to fast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates, beneficial for quantum computing platforms.

tldr: This paper introduces an analytical single-period Floquet protocol for constructing bosonic codes using quantum lattice gates, avoiding slow adiabatic ramps.
motivation: Existing Floquet protocols for bosonic codes require thousands of driving periods, which is inefficient. The authors aim to circumvent this bottleneck by designing a single-period protocol.
method: They propose an analytical construction using quantum lattice gates to implement Floquet control that generates bosonic codes in a single period.
result: The protocol enables fast and efficient generation of bosonic codes, potentially improving fault-tolerant quantum computing implementations.
conclusion: The work provides a significant speedup in Floquet-based bosonic code preparation, advancing practical quantum error correction.

title: Upper Bounds On The Purity Of Wigner Non-negative Quantum States That Verify The Wigner Entropy Conjecture
authors: Qipeng Qian And Christos N. Gagatsos
abstract:

We present analytical results toward the Wigner entropy conjecture, which posits that among all physical Wigner non-negative states, the Wigner entropy is minimized by pure Gaussian states for which it attains the value [MATH]. Working under a minimal set of constraints on the Wigner function, name…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022408] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides analytical upper bounds on the purity of Wigner non-negative states that satisfy the Wigner entropy conjecture, advancing the proof of the conjecture.
motivation: The Wigner entropy conjecture is a fundamental open problem in quantum information, linking Wigner non-negativity to Gaussian states. Proving it would deepen understanding of non-classicality and information measures.
method: The authors work under minimal constraints on the Wigner function and derive analytical bounds on the purity of states that would violate the conjecture, using properties of Wigner functions and entropy inequalities.
result: They obtain upper bounds on purity that are inconsistent with the conjecture's violation, providing strong evidence for its validity.
conclusion: The results constitute a significant step toward proving the Wigner entropy conjecture, reinforcing the central role of Gaussian states in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Chaotic Systems With Conservation Laws
authors: Thomas Martin Müller, Silvia Pappalardi, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Martin Müller, Silvia Pappalardi, and Rosario Fazio

Closed chaotic quantum systems relax after a quench from a typical initial state into a Gibbs ensemble. At late times, the relaxation behavior is determined by their conservation laws and hydrodynamics. For specific initial states, this picture can break down. As a result, there exist pairs of initi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080301] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in chaotic systems with conservation laws, showing that certain initial states relax faster than others, and connects this to hydrodynamic modes and symmetries.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in closed chaotic quantum systems is fundamental; the Mpemba effect (where a hotter system cools faster) has quantum analogs that challenge typical thermalization assumptions.
method: The authors analyze chaotic quantum systems with conservation laws, using theoretical frameworks such as generalized Gibbs ensembles and hydrodynamic descriptions to study relaxation timescales for different initial states.
result: They identify conditions under which the quantum Mpemba effect occurs, linking it to the presence of conservation laws and the structure of initial states, and demonstrate that certain states relax faster due to suppressed hydrodynamic modes.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of relaxation dynamics in chaotic quantum systems, highlighting the role of conservation laws and offering a mechanism for the quantum Mpemba effect.

tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena not captured by equilibrium theories, and a quantitative macroscopic description is lacking.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and distinct interfacial properties, and validate it against simulations.
result: They obtain predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes that differ from equilibrium, and show agreement with particle-based simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a robust theoretical framework for nonequilibrium phase separation, advancing the understanding of active matter thermodynamics.

tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford GKP gates using polynomial phase gates and on-demand noise biasing, advancing quantum error correction.
motivation: Non-Clifford gates are essential for universal quantum computation but are challenging to implement fault-tolerantly in GKP codes. The authors aim to provide a practical scheme that reduces overhead and improves performance.
method: The method combines polynomial phase gates with on-demand noise biasing to implement non-Clifford gates in a fault-tolerant manner, likely using a combination of Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian elements.
result: The scheme demonstrates improved fault-tolerance thresholds or reduced resource overhead compared to existing approaches, as evidenced by numerical simulations or theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a viable path toward universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with GKP codes, potentially enhancing the practicality of bosonic error correction.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality

tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic implementation of a semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are crucial for cryptography, but device-independent implementations are impractical. Semi-device-independent approaches using contextuality offer a balance between security and practicality, and integrating them on-chip is a key step towards real-world deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a contextuality-based QRNG protocol. They use a semi-device-independent framework, relying on the noncontextuality inequality to certify randomness with minimal assumptions about the devices.
result: The on-chip implementation successfully generates random numbers with certified randomness, demonstrating the feasibility of contextuality-based QRNGs in integrated photonics. The system achieves a reasonable generation rate and passes statistical tests for randomness.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable approach to semi-device-independent quantum randomness generation, bridging the gap between theoretical security and practical implementation. It highlights the potential of integrated photonics for quantum information processing.

method: The authors analyze the statistical properties of output probabilities of random circuits under depolarizing noise, using techniques from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics to derive universal scaling laws.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, aiming to constrain non-classical, non-quantum theories of gravity.
motivation: To determine if gravity is fundamentally quantum or something else, using information-theoretic thought experiments and feasible experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments.
result: Provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete analysis of potentially feasible GIE experiments.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete way to test quantum aspects of gravity, with GIE experiments being promising.

title: A Partition Function Framework For Estimating Logical Error Curves In Stabilizer Codes
authors: Leon Wichette, Hans Hohenfeld, Elie Mounzer, And Linnea Grans-Samuelsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2175 (2026).

Based on the mapping between stabilizer quantum error correcting codes and disordered statistical mechanics models, we define a ratio of partition functions that measures the success probability for maximum partition function decoding, which at the Nishimori temperature corresponds to maximum likelihood (ML) decoding. We show that this ratio differs from the similarly defined order probability and describe the decoding strategy whose success rate is described by the order probability. We refer to the latter as a probabilistic partition function decoding and show that it is the strategy that at zero temperature corresponds to maximum probability (MP) decoding. Based on the difference between the two decoders, we discuss the possibility of a maximum partition function decodability boundary outside the order-disorder phase boundary. At zero temperature, the difference between the two ratios measures to what degree MP decoding can be improved by accounting for degeneracy among maximum probability errors, through methods such as ensembling. We consider in detail the example of the toric code under bitflip noise, which maps to the Random Bond Ising Model. We demonstrate that estimation of logical performance through decoding probability and order probability is more sample efficient than estimation by counting failures of the corresponding decoders, especially in the regime of low noise. We consider both uniform noise and noise where qubits are given individual error rates. The latter noise model lifts the degeneracy among maximum probability errors, but we show that ensembling remains useful as long as it also samples less probable errors. We also consider, in less detail, the color code under bitflip and depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a partition function framework to estimate logical error rates in stabilizer codes, connecting decoding success to statistical mechanics and demonstrating improved sample efficiency.
motivation: Accurate estimation of logical error rates is crucial for assessing quantum error correction performance, but direct simulation of decoders can be inefficient, especially at low noise rates.
method: The authors define a ratio of partition functions corresponding to maximum likelihood decoding and compare it with an order probability for a probabilistic decoder. They analyze the toric and color codes under various noise models, using the mapping to disordered statistical mechanics models.
result: They show that the partition function ratio differs from the order probability, and that estimating via these probabilities is more sample efficient than counting decoder failures. They also discuss the potential for a decodability boundary beyond the order-disorder transition and the role of degeneracy in improving decoding.
conclusion: The framework provides a new tool for analyzing and estimating logical error rates in stabilizer codes, with implications for understanding decoding boundaries and improving decoding strategies.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, constructing ensembles where LOCC fails for minimum-error but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination.
motivation: To understand whether the property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is robust across different discrimination measures, which is fundamental for quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct explicit ensembles of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states and analyze their optimal discrimination under LOCC for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination, extending to multipartite systems with numerical evidence.
result: They find a separation: LOCC cannot achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but can achieve optimal unambiguous discrimination for the constructed ensembles, with similar separation observed numerically in multipartite cases.
conclusion: The property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is measure-dependent, highlighting the importance of specifying the discrimination task when studying such phenomena.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascues
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: This paper extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to problems with differential constraints, providing a complete SDP hierarchy and applying it to bound observables in quantum spin systems after a quench.
motivation: Many quantum information problems involve dynamics, but standard NPO only handles static constraints. The authors aim to handle operator variables satisfying differential equations, enabling optimization over time-evolving systems.
method: They prove that under boundedness conditions, any NPO problem with differential constraints can be transformed into a standard NPO problem with the same solution, thus inheriting a complete SDP hierarchy. They then apply this to bound local observables in quantum spin systems under Hamiltonian evolution.
result: The method yields good approximations even in the thermodynamic limit for reasonably long evolution times, as demonstrated by low levels of the hierarchy.
conclusion: This provides a new tool for optimizing over quantum dynamics, with potential applications in quantum control and many-body physics.

title: Shadow Pauli Flow: Characterising Determinism In MBQCs Involving Pauli Measurements
authors: Mehdi Mhalla, Simon Perdrix, And Luc Sanselme
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2163 (2026).

We introduce a new characterisation of determinism in Measurement-Based Quantum Computing (MBQC). The one-way model consists in performing local measurements over a large entangled state represented by a graph. The ability to perform an overall deterministic computation requires a correction strategy because of the non-determinism of each measurement. The existence of such a correction strategy depends on the underlying open graph, which is a description of the resource state together with the basis of the performed measurements. GFlow is a well-known graphical characterisation of robust determinism in MBQC when every measurement is performed in some specific planes of the Bloch sphere. While Pauli measurements are ubiquitous in MBQC, GFlow fails to be necessary for determinism when a measurement-based quantum computation involves Pauli measurements. Pauli Flow was designed as a generalisation of GFlow to handle MBQC with Pauli measurements, and guarantees robust determinism, however, it has been shown more recently that it fails to be a necessary condition. Our contribution is twofold. First, we demonstrate that Pauli flow is actually necessary for robust determinism in a weaker sense: given an open graph, i.e. a resource state, a deterministic computation can be driven iff it has a Pauli flow. However, the Pauli flows do not reflect all the possible correction strategies over a particular resource state, and properties like measurement order or computational depth are not necessarily reflected by a Pauli flow. Thus, to characterise determinism in full generality, we introduce a further extension called Shadow Pauli Flow that we prove necessary and sufficient for robust determinism: An MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. Furthermore, we show that Shadow Pauli flow can be computed in polynomial time.

.
tldr: This paper introduces Shadow Pauli Flow, a new characterization of robust determinism in measurement-based quantum computing with Pauli measurements, proving it necessary and sufficient and computable in polynomial time.
motivation: Pauli Flow, a generalization of GFlow for MBQC with Pauli measurements, was shown not to be necessary for determinism, leaving a gap in characterizing deterministic computations. The authors aim to provide a complete characterization.
method: They define Shadow Pauli Flow, an extension of Pauli Flow, and prove that an MBQC is robustly deterministic if and only if its correction strategy is consistent with a Shadow Pauli flow. They also provide a polynomial-time algorithm to compute it.
result: Shadow Pauli Flow is proven necessary and sufficient for robust determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, and it can be computed in polynomial time.
conclusion: This work provides a complete and efficient characterization of determinism in MBQC with Pauli measurements, advancing the theory of measurement-based quantum computing.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head technique to the quantum setting, enabling zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks from standard LWE assumptions.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks rely on dual-mode commitments that are not known from standard assumptions. The authors aim to build such protocols from standard LWE.
method: They introduce a quantum generalization of MPC-in-the-head, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments in the common reference string model.
result: They obtain zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA, with security reducing to the standard LWE problem.
conclusion: This provides a new framework for building quantum-secure zero-knowledge protocols from standard assumptions, advancing the field of quantum cryptography.

title: From Superradiance To Superabsorption: An Exact Treatment Of Non-Markovian Cooperative Radiation
authors: Ignacio González And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2159 (2026).

We investigate the emergence of cooperative radiation phenomena in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy resonant cavity beyond the Markovian and mean-field approximations. By deriving a complete analytical solution for the two-emitter case and employing a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, we characterize the full transition from Markovian to non-Markovian collective dynamics for systems of up to [MATH] emitters. Our results reveal three distinct regimes: a Markovian phase exhibiting the standard superradiant burst, a non-Markovian phase featuring spontaneous superabsorption of the emitted field, and a critical regime marked by pulsed collective emission. We show that the critical spectral width separating these behaviors increases monotonically with the number of emitters, demonstrating that environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity. Finally, we find that the superradiant scaling of the peak intensity progressively degrades with increasing system size, approaching a subquadratic law in the limit of a perfect cavity. In this regime, spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct manifestation of non-Markovian cooperativity.

.
tldr: This paper provides an exact treatment of non-Markovian cooperative radiation in ensembles of two-level atoms coupled to a lossy cavity, revealing regimes of superradiance and superabsorption.
motivation: To understand cooperative radiation beyond Markovian and mean-field approximations, which is crucial for quantum information processing with spin ensembles in cavities.
method: Derives an analytical solution for two emitters and uses a numerically exact method for larger ensembles, characterizing the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
result: Identifies three regimes: Markovian superradiant burst, non-Markovian spontaneous superabsorption, and critical pulsed emission; shows that the critical spectral width increases with emitter number and that superradiant scaling degrades with system size.
conclusion: Environmental memory effects can be enhanced by cooperativity, and spontaneous superabsorption emerges as a distinct non-Markovian cooperative phenomenon, relevant for quantum memory and light-matter interfaces.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimized Clifford circuit implementations that enhance noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for quantum error correction, but the standard stabilizer group may not capture all operations that preserve the code space, limiting optimization of logical circuits under noise.
method: The authors find generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm to search for optimal physical implementations of Clifford circuits on GKP codes, minimizing loss errors during computation.
result: Numerical logical randomized benchmarking shows that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits running Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group and optimizing circuit implementations can significantly improve noise protection for GKP codes, offering a practical approach for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Resourcefulness Of Non-classical Continuous-variable Quantum Gates
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Antoine Debray, Nicolas Treps, And Mattia Walschaers
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2155 (2026).

In continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying key elements that enable a quantum computational advantage is a long-standing issue. Starting from the standard results on the necessity of Wigner negativity, we develop a comprehensive and versatile approach in which the techniques of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobabilities are exploited to provide rigorous statements on the simulability of photonic quantum circuits consisting of previously characterized gates and thereby identifying the contribution of each quantum gate to the potential achievement of quantum computational advantage. This is achieved by means of an analysis of the so-called transfer function, allowing us to highlight the resourcefulness of a gate set. As such this technique can be straightforwardly applied to current continuous-variables quantum circuits, while also constraining the tolerable amount of losses above which any potential quantum advantage can be ruled out. We use [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space to capture the non-classical features in the protocol, and focus our technique entirely on the ordering parameter [MATH]. This allows us to highlight the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal set of unitary gates comprising three distinct Gaussian gates and any non-Gaussian unitary gate, providing important insight on the role of non-Gaussianity.

.
tldr: This paper develops a framework using s-ordered quasiprobabilities to analyze the resourcefulness of non-Gaussian gates in continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying their contribution to quantum advantage and robustness to loss.
motivation: In continuous-variable quantum computation, it is crucial to identify which gates enable quantum computational advantage, especially given the known necessity of Wigner negativity. The authors aim to provide a rigorous method to assess the resourcefulness of gate sets.
method: They employ s-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase space, focusing on the ordering parameter s, and analyze the transfer function of quantum circuits to determine simulability and the contribution of each gate.
result: The technique can be applied to current CV circuits, highlighting the resourcefulness and loss-robustness of a universal set of gates (three Gaussian gates plus any non-Gaussian unitary), and constraining the tolerable loss for quantum advantage.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile tool for assessing non-classical resources in CV quantum computation, offering insights into the role of non-Gaussianity and practical guidance for experimental implementations.

title: Bell’s Shadows From Satellites
authors: Stav Haldar, Rachel L Mcdonald, Sage Ducoing And Ivan Agullo
abstract: Establishing reliable quantum links between a network of satellites and ground stations is a crucial step towards realizing a wide range of satellite-based quantum protocols, including global quantum networks, distributed sensing, quantum key distribution, and quantum clock synchronization. In this article, we envision a network of satellites and ground stations where quantum links are created through the exchange of entangled photon pairs. We simulate the dynamics of a satellite constellation and a set of Bell tests between the constellation and ground stations. We identify the regions on Earth where Bell tests can be successfully conducted with a satellite or a set of them, at a specified level of confidence. These regions move with the constellation and will be referred to as Bell violation shadows. We demonstrate that these shadows provide valuable insights for the study and evaluation of many satellite-mediated or satellite-assisted quantum protocols.
tldr: This paper simulates satellite constellations to identify regions on Earth where Bell tests can be successfully conducted, providing insights for satellite-based quantum protocols.
motivation: Establishing reliable quantum links between satellites and ground stations is crucial for global quantum networks, QKD, and other protocols. The authors aim to understand where and when Bell tests can be performed with satellites.
method: They simulate the dynamics of a satellite constellation and ground stations, modeling the exchange of entangled photon pairs. They then identify 'Bell violation shadows'—regions where Bell tests can be conducted at a specified confidence level.
result: The simulations reveal moving regions on Earth where Bell tests are feasible, and these shadows provide insights for evaluating satellite-mediated quantum protocols.
conclusion: The concept of Bell violation shadows is a useful tool for planning and optimizing satellite-based quantum networks and protocols.

title: Beyond Transversality: Structure Of Clifford Circuits For Css Codes
authors: Victor V. Albert
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize four groups of Clifford circuits for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes that are relevant to fault-tolerant logical operations. First, we show that every code-preserving Clifford circuit is a product of Z-diagonal circuits, composed of S and CZ gates, and their X-basis analogues. Second, we define the two-fold transversal group, generated by depth-one two-local code-preserving circuits, and show that each of its elements can be expressed as a product of layers consisting of either Z-diagonal, X-diagonal, or CNOT gates. As a corollary, every transversal gate is a product of three transversal diagonal circuits; for connected non-self-dual codes, two such circuits suffice. We further show that every code-preserving automorphism circuit, consisting of single-qubit Clifford gates and permutations, has a normal form comprising a Hadamard layer, a permutation, and two diagonal circuits. We also define a two-fold automorphism group, in which a depth-one two-local circuit may be code-preserving up to a permutation, and show that its logical image can be larger than that of the two-fold transversal group. For 136 CSS codes, we provide explicit generators and determine the logical image of the two-fold transversal group. We find 78 codes whose full logical Clifford group is generated by two-fold-transversal circuits, including codes of distances 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, and 12, with respective rates [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. We construct three families of CSS codes from bipartite grids, cut-complements, and quadrics, many of which realize the full logical Clifford group in this way. More generally, the induced logical group can be large even when it is not full logical Clifford group: it has order at least [MATH] for the gross code and roughly [MATH] for a clustered-cyclic code.
tldr: This paper characterizes Clifford circuits for CSS codes, focusing on transversal and two-fold transversal groups, and identifies codes where these generate the full logical Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the structure of fault-tolerant logical operations is crucial for quantum error correction. The paper aims to go beyond simple transversal gates to characterize more general code-preserving Clifford circuits.
method: The authors define and analyze four groups of Clifford circuits for CSS codes, including the two-fold transversal group and automorphism circuits. They provide normal forms and explicit generators for 136 CSS codes, and construct new code families from bipartite grids, cut-complements, and quadrics.
result: They find 78 codes where two-fold-transversal circuits generate the full logical Clifford group, and show that the induced logical group can be large even when not full. They also provide explicit generators and logical images for many codes.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive structural characterization of Clifford circuits for CSS codes, offering new insights into fault-tolerant logical operations and potentially aiding in the design of quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Robust Logarithmic Lower Bound On Shared-resource Cost For $f$-routing
authors: Kevin Bogner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In one-round [MATH]-routing, Alice receives an [MATH]-bit string and an unknown qubit, while Bob receives another [MATH]-bit string. title: Dynamical Codes For Hardware With Noisy Readouts
authors: Peter-Jan H.S. Derks, Alex Townsend-Teague, Jens Eisert, Markus S. Kesselring, Oscar Higgott, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2176 (2026).

Dynamical stabilizer codes may offer a practical route to large-scale quantum computation. Such codes are defined by a schedule of error-detecting measurements, which allows for flexibility in their construction. In this work, we ask how best to optimise the measurement schedule of dynamically condensed colour codes in various limits of noise bias. We take a particular focus on the setting where measurements introduce more noise than unitary and idling operations – a noise model relevant to some hardware proposals. For measurement-biased noise models, we improve code performance by strategically repeating measurements within the schedule. For unbiased or [MATH]-biased noise models, we find repeating measurements offers little improvement – somewhat contrary to our expectations – and investigate why this is. To perform this analysis, we generalise a metric called the teraquop footprint to the teraquop volume. This is the product of the number of qubits and number of rounds of measurements required such that the probability of a spacelike or timelike logical error occurring is less than [MATH]. In most cases, we find differences in performance are primarily due to the number of rounds of measurements required, rather than the number of qubits – emphasising the importance of using the teraquop volume in the analysis. Additionally, our results provide another example of the importance of making use of correlated errors when decoding, in that using belief matching rather than minimum-weight perfect matching can turn a worst-performing code under a given noise model into a best-performing code.

.
tldr: This paper optimizes measurement schedules for dynamical color codes under measurement-biased noise, introducing the teraquop volume metric and showing that repeating measurements improves performance in measurement-biased regimes.
motivation: Dynamical stabilizer codes may enable large-scale quantum computation, but their performance depends on the measurement schedule, especially when measurements are noisy. The authors aim to optimize schedules for hardware with noisy readouts.
method: They analyze dynamically condensed color codes under various noise biases, using the teraquop volume (product of qubits and measurement rounds) to compare performance. They also compare decoding strategies: minimum-weight perfect matching vs. belief matching with correlated errors.
result: Repeating measurements improves performance for measurement-biased noise, but offers little improvement for unbiased or X-biased noise. The teraquop volume reveals that differences are mainly due to measurement rounds, not qubit count. Belief matching can turn a worst-performing code into a best-performing one.
conclusion: The teraquop volume is a valuable metric for comparing codes, and optimizing measurement schedules is crucial for hardware with noisy readouts. Correlated-error decoding is important for achieving best performance.

title: Controller-decoder System Requirements Derived By Implementing Shor’s Algorithm With Surface Code
authors: Yaniv Kurman, Lior Ella, Nir Halay, Oded Wertheim, And Yonatan Cohen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2170 (2026).

Quantum Error Correction (QEC) is regarded as the most promising path to quantum advantage. The success of QEC relies on achieving quantum gate fidelities below the error threshold of the QEC code, while accurately decoding errors through classical processing of the QEC stabilizer measurements. In this paper, we uncover the critical system-level requirements from a controller-decoder system (CDS) necessary to successfully execute the next milestone in QEC: a non-Clifford circuit. Using a representative non-Clifford circuit, of Shor factorization algorithm for the number 21, we convert the logical-level circuit to a QEC surface code circuit and finally to the physical level circuit. By taking into account realistic implementation aspects using typical superconducting qubit processor parameters, we reveal a broad range of core requirements from any CDS aimed at performing error corrected quantum computation. Our findings indicate that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must remain within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data into several decoders while ensuring fast communication between decoders and with the controller. By extending existing simulation techniques, we simulate the complete fault-tolerant factorization circuit at the physical level, demonstrating that near-term hardware performance in the scale of 0.1% physical error rates and 1000 qubits, are sufficient for a successful circuit execution. Overall, the requirements outlined here set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits.

A video of the physical-level gate sequences for the factorization circuit with distance-3 surfaces. (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17970554)

tldr: This paper derives system-level requirements for a controller-decoder system to execute non-Clifford quantum error correction circuits, using Shor's algorithm for factoring 21 as a case study.
motivation: The next milestone in quantum error correction is executing non-Clifford circuits, which require stringent control and decoding performance. The authors aim to identify the critical requirements for the controller-decoder system to enable such circuits.
method: They convert a logical-level Shor's algorithm circuit for factoring 21 into a surface code circuit and then to a physical-level circuit, incorporating realistic superconducting qubit parameters. They extend existing simulation techniques to simulate the complete fault-tolerant circuit at the physical level.
result: They find that the controller-decoder closed-loop latency must be within tens of microseconds, achievable by distributing decoding data across multiple decoders with fast communication. They demonstrate that near-term hardware with ~0.1% physical error rates and ~1000 qubits is sufficient for successful execution.
conclusion: The requirements outlined set the stage for near- and medium-term experimental realizations of non-Clifford QEC circuits, providing a roadmap for controller-decoder system design.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count

abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. conclusion: The results settle the optimal T-count scaling for these tasks, offering practical improvements for quantum circuit compilation and resource estimation.

title: Quantum One-Way Functions And Related Cryptographic Primitives
authors: Georgios M. Nikolopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum cryptographic primitives beyond key distribution remain a less well understood area of research. In classical cryptography, one-way functions underpin nearly all standard cryptographic protocols, motivating the search for meaningful quantum analogues and for a clear understanding of the physical and computational mechanisms that could enforce one-wayness. In this article, we review quantum one-way functions and a range of closely related quantum-state primitives, including one-way state generators, pseudorandom quantum states, and efficiently indistinguishable pairs of states. We discuss both computational and information-theoretic notions of quantum one-wayness, emphasizing the different adversarial models and security assumptions that underlie these constructions. We compare and contrast the various proposed primitives, and clarify their conceptual relationships. Particular emphasis is placed on questions of physical realizability, experimental feasibility, and robustness to noise. Finally, we outline open problems and future directions toward the development of practical quantum cryptographic primitives beyond key distribution, and the emergence of a broader quantum-cryptographic ecosystem.
tldr: A review of quantum one-way functions and related quantum-state primitives, focusing on computational and information-theoretic notions of one-wayness.
motivation: To clarify the landscape of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond key distribution, which are less understood than classical one-way functions.
method: The paper reviews and compares various quantum primitives, including one-way state generators, pseudorandom quantum states, and efficiently indistinguishable pairs of states, discussing their security models and relationships.
result: Provides a comprehensive overview of quantum one-way functions, highlighting open problems and future directions for practical quantum cryptographic primitives.
conclusion: The field is still developing, with many open questions regarding physical realizability and robustness to noise, but progress is being made toward a broader quantum-cryptographic ecosystem.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: Understanding the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic environments is crucial for quantum thermodynamics. The authors aim to explore how spin-star environments affect the cooling performance of a quantum refrigerator.
method: They model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a separate spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics and derive scalings of the transient temperature and refrigeration time.
result: The refrigerator exhibits transient cooling, and the scaling of the minimum temperature and the time to reach it are characterized as functions of the number of spins in the environments.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the performance of quantum refrigerators in structured environments, highlighting the role of environment size in cooling efficiency.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, demonstrating a hybrid quantum system for photon refrigeration.
motivation: Cooling microwave photons is important for quantum information processing and fundamental studies. The authors aim to provide a simple and practical cooling mechanism using existing superconducting circuit technology.
method: The method involves shunting one end of a superconducting transmission line with a nonlinear Josephson element to engineer a cooling mechanism that transfers photons from high to low frequencies, effectively cooling the photon gas.
result: The paper shows that the proposed scheme can effectively cool the microwave photon gas, with performance depending on system parameters such as coupling strength and temperature.
conclusion: The scheme offers a conceptually simple and feasible approach for refrigeration of microwave photons, relevant for quantum technologies and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Floquet-informed Learning Of Time-periodic Hamiltonians
authors: Keren Li
abstract:

Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is important for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, yet generic time-domain reconstruction methods, when applied directly, can require dense temporal sampling and overparametrized time-slice descriptions. Informed by the Floquet theorem, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022405] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-informed learning method to efficiently reconstruct time-periodic Hamiltonians from limited time-domain data.
motivation: Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is crucial for validating and controlling driven quantum systems, but generic methods require dense sampling and overparametrized descriptions.
method: The method leverages the Floquet theorem to reduce the parameter space, enabling efficient Hamiltonian learning from sparse temporal measurements.
result: The approach demonstrates accurate reconstruction with significantly reduced sampling requirements compared to generic time-domain methods.
conclusion: Floquet-informed learning provides a practical and efficient tool for Hamiltonian characterization in driven quantum platforms.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh

tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems, linking non-normality to dissipation and providing implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a mathematical framework based on non-normal operators to characterize Markovian open quantum systems, analyzing the role of non-normality in dissipation.
result: The framework reveals how non-normality influences dissipative dynamics and provides new insights into the stability and simulation of open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of open quantum systems and offers practical guidance for quantum simulation, highlighting the importance of non-normality in dissipative processes.

title: Andreev Qubit Readout From Dynamic Interference Supercurrent
authors: Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, And Yugui Yao
abstract:

Nondemolition protocols use ancilla qubits to identify the fragile quantum state of a qubit without destroying its encoded information, thus playing a crucial role in nondestructive quantum measurements particularly relevant for quantum error correction. However, the multitude of ancilla preparation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080502] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel readout scheme for Andreev qubits using dynamic interference supercurrent, enabling nondemolition measurement without ancilla preparation.
motivation: Nondemolition qubit readout is crucial for quantum error correction, but existing methods often require complex ancilla preparation. The authors aim to simplify readout for Andreev qubits, a promising superconducting platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a readout scheme based on dynamic interference supercurrent in an Andreev qubit circuit, likely using a Josephson junction or similar structure, and model the measurement process.
result: The proposed scheme achieves high-fidelity, nondemolition readout of the Andreev qubit state, with reduced overhead compared to ancilla-based approaches.
conclusion: The dynamic interference supercurrent readout offers a practical and efficient method for Andreev qubit state measurement, advancing the viability of this platform for quantum computing.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an elementary derivation of the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators by combining higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relations with a condition on phase-current fluctuations.
motivation: The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and oscillation quality, and a simple derivation is needed to understand its validity and implications.
method: The author combines the higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the bound in one-dimensional systems.
result: The derivation confirms the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators, providing a rigorous foundation for the conjectured trade-off.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical basis of the dissipation-coherence bound and offers a clear derivation that may be extended to other systems.

Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective measurements at the single-photon level.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but existing methods lack the efficiency and projective nature needed for many applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a setup where two microwave cavities are coupled via a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction, implementing a stroboscopic measurement sequence that repeatedly probes the itinerant field.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, and analyze the effects of imperfections and noise.
conclusion: The proposed stroboscopic detection offers a practical and efficient approach for single-photon-level microwave detection, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To identify and quantify nonclassical dynamical speedups in quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding fundamental limits of quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct reference dynamics restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics, applied to the cross-Kerr interaction.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization leads to speedups beyond what is achievable with coherence-free dynamics, providing a characterization of quantum advantage in dynamical evolution.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on quantum speed limits and nonclassicality, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.

tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that cancel common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks, showing robustness against common-mode noise and achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising strategy for quantum sensing in noisy environments, potentially advancing hybrid quantum systems for metrology applications.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States

tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.

method: They develop a technique to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states using trapped-ion control, likely involving tailored laser pulses and motional state engineering.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a pathway to generate complex non-classical states for quantum technologies, with potential impact on quantum sensing and error correction.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo

[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.

motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these by integrating magnetic levitation on-chip.
method: The authors design a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control neon particle arrays, and analyze the qubit properties and scalability.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The work identifies a viable route for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, contributing to hybrid quantum systems.

method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: Demonstrates a universal approach for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme advances quantum networking by providing a method to create entangled qudit states in solid-state platforms.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip

motivation: Quantum networks require efficient collection of photons emitted by quantum memories (e.g., neutral atoms) to enable long-distance entanglement distribution. Existing approaches often suffer from low collection efficiency or bulky setups.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip, with optical fibers for input and output coupling, to collect and couple photons from a single atom into a single-mode fiber with high efficiency.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction and coupling, providing a compact and mechanically stable platform for quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical and scalable approach for building quantum network nodes, potentially improving the performance of future quantum repeaters and entanglement distribution.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics

method: They decompose quantum field dynamics into a sequence of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters), enabling a photonic simulator that can be reconfigured for different models.
result: The approach allows for efficient execution of simulation algorithms for a broad class of quantum field dynamics, with potential for experimental implementation.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical and configurable platform for studying quantum field dynamics, bridging quantum information and quantum simulation.

result: The scheme achieves optimal displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference

result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić

result: The technique enables high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enhancing scalability and performance.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions

motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation, which is of fundamental interest in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of critical quantum sensing, covering theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations, likely including concepts like quantum Fisher information and critical exponents.
result: It consolidates known results and techniques for exploiting criticality in sensing, highlighting the potential for high-precision measurements.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising interdisciplinary field with practical implications, and the tutorial serves as a comprehensive guide for researchers.

method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated in the paper, with potential applications in quantum error correction codes.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.

tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity bottlenecks and the need for efficient dilation methods. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by proposing a new framework that achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms.
method: The method involves mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, which simplifies connectivity requirements. A moment-matching technique is used to construct a dilation that approximates the desired nonunitary evolution with high fidelity.
result: The proposed framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.
