tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique for fast quantum control, but variational approaches often suffer from low fidelity. The authors aim to enhance fidelity by refining the variational ansatz.
method: They propose a weighted action functional that emphasizes important terms and use computer algebra to systematically construct better variational ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical examples.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical upgrade to existing variational counterdiabatic driving, improving quantum control performance.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit universal nonequilibrium stationary states relevant to modern experiments, but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behaviors using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: The review provides a comprehensive classification of universality classes in driven open quantum matter.
conclusion: This work consolidates theoretical understanding and highlights open questions in the field.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on spin-spin relaxation.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly reliable for predicting spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: Modulator-Assisted Zeno Control Of Energy Transfer In Quantum Batteries
authors: Songbo Xie, Manas Sajjan, Ashok Ajoy, And Sabre Kais
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2178 (2026).

Efficient operation of quantum batteries requires not only fast energy transfer but also the ability to halt the charging process to prevent reverse flow. Existing approaches typically rely on direct control of the charger-battery interaction, which can be experimentally demanding. Here we propose a modulator-assisted quantum battery protocol that enables indirect control of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on. By applying repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, we exploit a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the charger-battery coupling on and off. We demonstrate this mechanism in a minimal three-body model and show that it remains effective beyond the ideal fast-control limit. We further extend the protocol to a collective many-body architecture, where it preserves the characteristic enhancement of charging power, scaling as [MATH] with the number of battery units. We also discuss a possible implementation in an NV-[MATH]C spin platform. Our results establish modulator-assisted Zeno control as a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a modulator-assisted Zeno control protocol for quantum batteries, enabling indirect on/off switching of energy transfer while keeping the interaction always on.
motivation: Efficient quantum battery operation requires halting charging to prevent reverse flow, but direct control of the charger-battery interaction is experimentally demanding. The authors aim to achieve indirect control via a modulator qubit.
method: They apply repeated local unitary operations to an auxiliary modulator qubit, exploiting a Zeno-like mechanism to dynamically reshape the effective Hamiltonian and switch the coupling on/off. They analyze a minimal three-body model and extend to a collective many-body architecture, also discussing an NV-13C implementation.
result: The mechanism works beyond the ideal fast-control limit and preserves the collective charging power enhancement scaling with the number of battery units.
conclusion: Modulator-assisted Zeno control offers a scalable route to regulating energy transfer in quantum batteries, potentially easing experimental requirements.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper establishes tight worst-case program costs for programming low-depth brickwork circuits, showing that gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.
motivation: Efficiently programming NISQ devices is crucial for realizing quantum advantages, but existing methods for generic unitary transformations are inefficient for low-depth circuits.
method: The authors analyze the circuit complexity and quantum memory size (program cost) required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using the light-cone argument to trade off layout description cost and programming cost.
result: They establish a tight worst-case program cost for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-qubit regime, and show that gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
conclusion: The findings provide fundamental limits on the resources needed to program low-depth quantum circuits, guiding the design of efficient programming strategies for NISQ devices.

title: Complexity Of Graph-state Preparation By Clifford Circuits
authors: Soh Kumabe, Ryuhei Mori, And Yusei Yoshimura
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2165 (2026).

In this work, we study the complexity of graph-state preparation in a general model of quantum algorithms that allows measurements in the computational basis, single-qubit Clifford operations, and two-qubit Clifford operations. We define the CZ-complexity of a graph state [MATH] as the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations required to generate [MATH] from [MATH] for some [MATH]. Equivalently, every optimal algorithm can be taken to use only controlled-Z (CZ) gates as its two-qubit Clifford operations. We then give a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations. Specifically, [MATH] can be generated from another graph state [MATH] by an algorithm of CZ-complexity at most [MATH] if and only if [MATH] can be obtained from [MATH] by vertex deletions, local complementations and at most [MATH] elementary edge-complementations. Here, an elementary edge-complementation toggles either a single edge, all edges between one vertex and the neighborhood of another, or all edges between the neighborhoods of two non-adjacent vertices. Using this characterization, we relate CZ-complexity to rank-width. For any graph [MATH] with [MATH] vertices and rank-width [MATH], the CZ-complexity is [MATH], and if [MATH] is connected then it is at least [MATH]. We also show that these bounds are close to optimal. Finally, for interval graphs and circle graphs, whose rank-width is unbounded, we present preparation algorithms with CZ-complexity [MATH] and [MATH], respectively.

tldr: This paper characterizes the minimum number of two-qubit Clifford operations (CZ-complexity) needed to prepare graph states, linking it to rank-width and providing algorithms for interval and circle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of preparing graph states is crucial for quantum information processing, as graph states are key resources for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors define CZ-complexity and prove a combinatorial characterization of graph-state transformations using vertex deletions, local complementations, and edge-complementations. They then relate this complexity to rank-width and provide preparation algorithms for specific graph classes.
result: They show that for any graph with n vertices and rank-width r, the CZ-complexity is O(n*r) and at least Ω(n*r) for connected graphs. They also give O(n) and O(n log n) algorithms for interval and circle graphs, respectively.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for quantifying graph-state preparation complexity, with implications for optimizing quantum circuits and understanding the power of Clifford operations.

title: Geometric Speed Limit Of State Preparation And Curved Control Spaces
authors: Maximilian Goll And Robert H. Jonsson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2160 (2026).

The preparation of quantum many-body systems faces the difficulty that in a realistic scenario only few control parameters of the system may be accessible. In this context, an interesting connection between the energy fluctuations during state preparation and its geometric length as measured by the Fubini-Study metric was discussed by Bukov et al. in 2019 [5]. An inspiring conjecture lower bounding the energy fluctuations by the minimal geometric length of all accessible state preparation protocols was put forward together with supporting examples and numerical evidence. However, we here show that the conjecture does not hold but can be violated if the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature, when embedded into the space of all dynamically accessible states. We illustrate this by a number of generic qubit, qutrit and harmonic oscillator systems.

.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture on geometric speed limits for state preparation, showing that extrinsic curvature of control spaces can lead to violations.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the fundamental limits on the speed of quantum state preparation when only few control parameters are accessible, building on a conjecture by Bukov et al. that relates energy fluctuations to geometric length.
method: They analyze the conjecture using the Fubini-Study metric and demonstrate violations through explicit examples in qubit, qutrit, and harmonic oscillator systems where the accessible parameter space has extrinsic curvature.
result: The conjecture is shown to be false in general; violations occur when the control space is curved when embedded in the full state space.
conclusion: The geometric speed limit is not universally valid, and the role of curvature must be considered in characterizing state preparation efficiency.

title: Theory Of Measurement-Altered Criticality
authors: Kabir Khanna, Sara Murciano, Romain Vasseur
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local measurements can alter long-range correlations in gapless quantum matter. We propose a theory of weakly-monitored Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, a broad class of quantum critical states in one dimension. In order to address the intrinsic randomness of the measurement record, we develop a replica instanton calculation to study Born-averaged observables. We find that when measurements are relevant, average correlators of density and phase fluctuations decay at long distances as universal power laws with logarithmic corrections, a feature we argue is peculiar to measurement-induced randomness. We characterize the full multifractal spectrum of moments of correlations functions, revealing broad, strongly non-gaussian fluctuations across the ensemble of post-measurement states. We support these analytic results with matrix-product-state calculations, and provide a general picture of measurement-altered criticality for ground states described by 1+1d conformal field theories. Our results establish that physical measurements alter critical quantum states in a manner that lies beyond both forced measurements and conventional critical scaling.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of measurement-altered criticality in weakly-monitored Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, showing that measurements induce universal power-law decays with logarithmic corrections and multifractal fluctuations.
motivation: To understand how local measurements alter long-range correlations in gapless quantum matter, beyond forced measurements and conventional critical scaling.
method: Uses a replica instanton calculation for Born-averaged observables and supports with matrix-product-state simulations.
result: Finds universal power-law decays with logarithmic corrections in average correlators, and a broad multifractal spectrum of moments, indicating strong non-Gaussian fluctuations.
conclusion: Measurement-induced randomness fundamentally alters critical quantum states, providing a general picture for 1+1d CFTs.

title: Identifying Slow Relaxation In Many-body Quantum Systems Through State-graph Geometry And State-graph Heterogeneity
authors: Tom Ben-Ami Heiko Georg Menzler
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We adapt tools from the theory of quantum random walks to investigate slow relaxation dynamics through the many-body state graph. Specifically, we construct a probe of heterogeneity between basis states defined using hitting times derived from the unitary time-evolution operator. We find that the state-graph geometry, encoded by the pairwise hitting time of basis states, is a highly sensitive indicator of slow relaxation dynamics in a variety of systems. We study three paradigmatic models: the Rosenzweig-Porter model, the quantum East model, and the triangular lattice gas model, exhibiting a sudden onset of slow dynamics upon tuning of a control parameter. As a global characterization of the graph geometry, we analyze the spectral radius of the hitting matrix. We find that it increases sharply at the onset of slow dynamics, spanning many orders of magnitude, with a characteristic crossing point at the transition. Our work provides a geometric framework for describing and identifying phases with slow relaxation using a unified graph-theoretic formalism.
tldr: This paper introduces a graph-theoretic framework based on quantum random walk hitting times to identify slow relaxation phases in many-body quantum systems.
motivation: Slow relaxation dynamics in many-body quantum systems are often difficult to characterize. The authors aim to provide a unified geometric probe that can detect the onset of slow dynamics across different models.
method: They construct a state graph where basis states are nodes and edges are weighted by hitting times derived from the unitary time-evolution operator. They analyze the spectral radius of the hitting matrix as a global measure of graph heterogeneity.
result: The spectral radius increases sharply at the onset of slow dynamics, spanning orders of magnitude, with a characteristic crossing point at the transition, as demonstrated in the Rosenzweig-Porter, quantum East, and triangular lattice gas models.
conclusion: The state-graph geometry provides a sensitive and unified indicator of slow relaxation, offering a new tool for identifying dynamical phases in quantum systems.

title: Unidirectional Dark-to-Bright Rescue In Cavity-Coupled Quantum Transport
authors: Jack Diab, Arpit Arora, Taylor L. Patti, Prineha Narang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical microcavities can transport energy ballistically across an emitter array, but the same coupling buries most of the excitation in a manifold of dark states that grows with system size and traps energy outside the transport channel. We show that the off-diagonal (non-Condon) part of the exciton-phonon coupling opens a one-way escape route from this trap, driving population irreversibly from dark states into the radiative channel. This rate is fixed by a photonic-weight conservation law rather than by dark-bright overlap which evacuates the dark manifold at a rate independent of system size. The mechanism contributes to transport with near-complete efficiency with four signatures being single exponential dark state decay, a size scaling efficiency gap, distinct temperature behavior, and a resonance in the escape rate at vibrational bath modes. Beyond polariton transport, it recasts dark states from a parasitic loss channel into an engineered dissipative resource, with implications for light harvesting and dissipation based quantum control.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Condon exciton-phonon coupling in cavity-coupled emitter arrays provides a size-independent, one-way escape route from dark states into the radiative channel, enabling near-complete transport efficiency.
motivation: Strong light-matter coupling in microcavities can transport energy ballistically, but dark states trap excitation and reduce efficiency. The authors aim to understand and exploit the mechanism that can rescue population from these dark states.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a model of cavity-coupled quantum emitters with exciton-phonon coupling, focusing on the off-diagonal (non-Condon) part. They derive a photonic-weight conservation law that determines the escape rate and identify four signatures of the mechanism.
result: The non-Condon coupling drives irreversible population transfer from dark states to the radiative channel at a rate independent of system size, leading to near-complete transport efficiency. The mechanism exhibits single exponential dark state decay, a size scaling efficiency gap, distinct temperature behavior, and a resonance at vibrational bath modes.
conclusion: The work recasts dark states from a parasitic loss to an engineered dissipative resource, with implications for light harvesting and dissipation-based quantum control.

title: Machine Learning For Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization: Generative Configuration Recovery And The Classical-simulability Frontier
authors: Nicol\'as Bonilla Vargas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), equivalently quantum-selected configuration interaction (QSCI), has in two years become a pragmatic centre of gravity of pre-fault-tolerant quantum chemistry: a quantum processor samples electronic configurations, and the many-electron Hamiltonian is diagonalized classically in the resulting determinant subspace. Its accuracy is set entirely by which configurations enter that subspace, a selection problem for machine learning made acute by a coupon-collector bottleneck. We critically review the ecosystem of generative and learned selectors, organizing it by the object each method generates and the importance signal it exploits, and expose one conspicuous gap: a reward-proportional generative-flow-network proposer built for tail discovery. We then confront the field's central question -- whether the quantum sampler beats classical selected configuration interaction -- and report a carefully scoped negative: across published same-active-space comparisons, strong classical selected CI matches or beats the quantum-sampled subspace, and the flagship single-layer circuits now admit polynomial-time classical energy estimation. We distil a benchmarking standard and turn the negative into a regime map, then test it with FCI-exact experiments that confirm one prediction and refute another: the cheap prior's rank correlation with the exact weights declines with multireference character (a usable coordinate), but a controlled single-molecule noise sweep shows the one generative advantage we find, robustness to valid-shot starvation, to be generic rather than the multireference-specific effect a confounded contrast first suggested. Finally, we flag learning from quantum experiments, whose classical sample-complexity lower bound is an unconditional theorem, as the one adjacent frontier where a quantum advantage is provable but not yet bridged to chemistry.
tldr: This paper reviews and benchmarks machine learning methods for sample-based quantum diagonalization in quantum chemistry, finding that classical selected CI often matches or beats quantum sampling, and identifies a provable quantum advantage in learning from quantum experiments.
motivation: The accuracy of sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) depends on the selection of electronic configurations, which is a machine learning problem. The field needs a critical review and benchmarking to determine whether quantum sampling offers an advantage over classical methods.
method: The authors organize generative and learned selectors by the object they generate and the importance signal used, propose a reward-proportional generative flow network for tail discovery, and conduct FCI-exact experiments to test predictions about rank correlation and noise robustness.
result: Strong classical selected CI matches or beats quantum-sampled subspaces in published comparisons, and single-layer circuits admit polynomial-time classical energy estimation. The cheap prior's rank correlation declines with multireference character, and a noise sweep shows a generative advantage in robustness to valid-shot starvation is generic.
conclusion: The paper establishes a benchmarking standard and a regime map, refuting a multireference-specific effect, and highlights learning from quantum experiments as a frontier where quantum advantage is provable but not yet bridged to chemistry.

title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem In Semidirect Products And Quasi-Hamiltonian Groups
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several early quantum algorithms, including Simon's algorithm and Shor's period-finding are instances of the hidden subgroup problem (HSP) over finite abelian groups. No polynomial-time quantum algorithm is known for the HSP over arbitrary non-abelian finite groups. The non-Abelian case is of particular interest because some instances, such as the dihedral and symmetric group HSPs, are connected to lattice problems and graph isomorphism, respectively. In this work, we give polynomial-time quantum algorithms for two further families containing non-Abelian groups. First, we consider groups of the form [MATH], with [MATH] finite Abelian, [MATH] prime, [MATH] and the action of [MATH] is generated by the scalar automorphism [MATH], for some [MATH], where [MATH] is the exponent of [MATH]. Our algorithm is efficient when [MATH] has bounded generator rank and [MATH]. This includes the case [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH], studied by Bacon, Childs and van Dam (FOCS 2005), and [MATH] with [MATH] prime and [MATH] studied by van Dam and Dey (TQC 2014). Second, we give a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for finite quasi-Hamiltonian groups under a mild assumption on the input structure. Quasi-Hamiltonian groups are finite nilpotent groups with modular subgroup lattice, or equivalently the finite groups in which every subgroup is permutable. As far as we know, this is the first quantum algorithm to exploit the modularity of the subgroup lattice for solving the HSP. This extends, under the aforementioned structured input assumption, the quantum algorithm for Dedekind groups given by Hallgren, Russell, and Ta-Shma (SIAM J. Comput. 32, 2003).

title: QBism On Locality And Nonlocality
authors: John B. Debrota, Christopher A. Fuchs, R\"udiger Schack
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently Pienaar (2026), building on work of Cavalcanti (2021), has shown that QBism cannot always assume distinct observers' quantum-measurement outcomes---say, of Wigner and his friend---are embedded in a single spacetime. This follows from QBism's rejection of the `Absoluteness of Observed Events' assumption in the Bong et al. no-go theorem. Thus, QBism has no choice but to treat the notion of spacetime every bit as personalistic as it treats quantum states and quantum measurement outcomes. In a way, this is not a surprise to QBists, as they have taken the notion of `personalist spacetimes' to be the ansatz most compatible with their other views since at least 2009. But it does enjoin us to finally make crystal clear the sense in which QBism is a purely local interpretation of quantum mechanics despite this new theorem and despite quantum theory's age-old violation of Bell's inequalities. With the extra clarity we also hope to poise QBism for a distinctly new way to approach issues at the interface of quantum theory and gravity.

result: They conclude that QBism is a purely local interpretation, with spacetime being personalistic, and suggest this perspective may offer new approaches to quantum gravity.

title: Quantum Error Mitigation With Diffusion-Like Models
authors: Yuval Idan, Ofek Nourian, Elad Mentovich, Taylor L. Patti, Eliahu Cohen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coupling between a quantum system and its environment causes decoherence by transferring information from the system to environmental degrees of freedom. When discretized in time, such interactions can be interpreted as sequences of weak measurements that provide an effective model of noisy quantum dynamics. Motivated by this picture, we propose an AI-assisted error-mitigation framework for quantum diffusion processes generated by sequential local weak measurements. The forward process progressively erases information from the input state through weak measurements performed in randomly selected Pauli bases, producing basis-dependent local dephasing and locally depolarizing dynamics on average. Machine-learning models are trained on exact synthetic density matrices to learn a channel- and distribution-specific denoising map and estimate the corresponding pre-noise state. We benchmark the approach on single-qubit states and separable and entangled multi-qubit registers. We also study distribution-dependent local-to-global reconstruction, in which local reduced density matrices are used to reconstruct the global state. This experimentally motivated setting relies on locally accessible information and is therefore compatible with noisy and distributed quantum systems. More broadly, the framework provides a hybrid classical-quantum approach for approximating non-unitary dynamics and mitigating coherence loss.
tldr: This paper proposes an AI-assisted error mitigation framework for quantum systems undergoing weak measurement-induced decoherence, using diffusion-like models to denoise quantum states.
motivation: Quantum systems suffer from decoherence due to environment coupling, which can be modeled as sequences of weak measurements. The authors aim to mitigate this noise using machine learning, providing a hybrid classical-quantum approach.
method: The forward process applies random Pauli weak measurements to erase information, and a neural network is trained on synthetic density matrices to learn a denoising map that estimates the pre-noise state. They benchmark on single and multi-qubit states, including local-to-global reconstruction.
result: The framework successfully mitigates errors for single-qubit and multi-qubit states, including entangled states, and demonstrates that local reduced density matrices can be used to reconstruct global states, making it compatible with distributed systems.
conclusion: The work provides a novel hybrid approach for approximating non-unitary dynamics and mitigating coherence loss, with potential applications in noisy quantum systems.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of The Quantum Fourier Transform On Up To 100 Qubits Using A Convolutional Compilation Strategy
authors: Paul Coote, Michael J. Biercuk, Yuval Baum
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present and experimentally validate the `Convolutional QFT': a constructive compilation strategy for the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) subroutine on a linear nearest neighbor (LNN) qubit topology. We first introduce a novel strategy that compiles the [MATH]-qubit QFT onto an LNN topology using only [MATH] [MATH] gates, matching requirements of a direct compilation on an all-to-all architecture. We then derive the convolutional variant used in our experiments, which requires an additional two [MATH] gates in total, and is realized via a compact, translation-invariant kernel circuit gadget that traverses a quantum register. We demonstrate the power of the convolutional compilation strategy on the IBM Quantum Platform by executing QFT benchmarking circuits. We measure a process fidelity of 11.4% at 50 qubits, and 1.8% at 80 qubits. The correct output state remains clearly distinguishable above background noise up to 100 qubits. These results constitute the largest experimental QFT demonstrated on any quantum computing hardware to date.
tldr: This paper presents a novel compilation strategy for the Quantum Fourier Transform on linear nearest neighbor topologies and demonstrates it experimentally on up to 100 qubits, setting a record for QFT implementation.
motivation: The Quantum Fourier Transform is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its implementation on near-term hardware with limited connectivity is challenging. The authors aim to provide an efficient compilation method that reduces gate count and enables large-scale experimental demonstrations.
method: They introduce a 'Convolutional QFT' compilation strategy that uses a translation-invariant kernel circuit gadget to implement the QFT on a linear nearest neighbor (LNN) topology with only O(n^2) gates, matching all-to-all connectivity requirements. They then execute benchmarking circuits on IBM Quantum Platform.
result: They measure process fidelities of 11.4% at 50 qubits and 1.8% at 80 qubits, with the correct output state distinguishable above noise up to 100 qubits, marking the largest experimental QFT to date.
conclusion: The convolutional compilation strategy enables scalable QFT implementation on current hardware, demonstrating feasibility for large-scale quantum algorithms despite noise, and provides a practical approach for near-term quantum computing.

title: What Meter Interference Can Tell Us About The Statistics Of Weak Measurements
authors: Holger F. Hofmann, Tomonori Matsushita, Masayoshi Isobe, Jonte R. Hance
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is widely assumed that the quantum fluctuations of the meter readout in a weak measurement make it impossible to identify the contributions originating from the individual values of the physical property observed in the measurement. Here, we show that a careful analysis of the quantum dynamics of the meter system allows us to identify a universal relation between quantum interference in the post-selection probability, and quantum interference in the statistics of the meter readout. The analysis reveals that quantum interference modifies the readout distribution of the meter in two ways, a diffusion term that identifies the appropriate operator ordering in the post-selected variance of the observed system property, and a wavefunction-dependent update of the initial meter statistics based on the effect of back action on the post-selection probability. Our results show that the statistical patterns described by meter interference provide important details about the physics of post-selection in weak measurements, allowing us to exclude the possibility of statistical artefacts in the experimental observation of weak values.

method: The authors perform a careful analysis of the quantum dynamics of the meter system, deriving a universal relation between quantum interference in the post-selection probability and interference in the meter readout distribution, identifying diffusion and back-action effects.
result: They find that meter interference modifies the readout distribution in two ways: a diffusion term that determines operator ordering in the post-selected variance, and a wavefunction-dependent update of initial meter statistics due to back action on post-selection probability.
conclusion: The results show that meter interference provides important details about the physics of post-selection in weak measurements, ruling out statistical artifacts in experimental observations of weak values.

title: Generating Two-mechanical Mode Entangled Cat States, And Steady-state Entanglement, In Cavity Optomechanics In The Presence Of Dissipation
authors: Jason Twamley Sanket Das
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a dissipation-engineering approach to produce a phase-dependent collective-mode Schr\"odinger cat state involving two modes. Our model features a single cavity mode that interacts with two spectrally identical mechanical oscillators. Both oscillators are coupled through a phase-dependent hopping interaction. We demonstrate that by adjusting the phase of the phonon-hopping interaction, one can control the bipartite entanglement of the phase-dependent two-mode cat state during its generation. Additionally, our study reveals that phonon interactions act as a tunable parameter, enabling the manipulation of steady-state entanglement between the bare mechanical modes, even in the presence of environmental effects and thermal excitations. Our scheme provides a feasible approach for the phase-dependent multi mode non-Gaussian states preparation.

title: X-z Round Scheduling For The Surface Code With Defects Under Biased Noise
authors: Lakshika Rathi, Pau Escofet, Joshua Viszlai, Margaret Martonosi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05518v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) relies on Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes that encode logical qubits across many physical qubits to detect and correct errors. The surface code is among the most widely studied codes due to its high error threshold, the existence of efficient decoders, and hardware-friendly properties: a planar, two-dimensional layout with nearest-neighbor connectivity. In practice, however, the fabrication of solid-state quantum processors introduces hardware defects, resulting in defective qubits and couplers that must be discarded. Adapting the surface code to these defects often requires measuring the [MATH]- and [MATH]-type checks in separate rounds rather than simultaneously. In this work, we investigate the optimal [MATH]-to-[MATH] checks round-scheduling ratio under biased noise systems. Our results characterize how key architectural parameters, such as noise bias, code distance, and defect rate, impact the logical error rate. We provide insights into how to determine the optimal scheduling ratio directly from device calibration data, enabling manufacturers to maximize performance without extensive simulations. Our approach reduces the logical error rate by up to [MATH] at a [MATH] defect rate and up to [MATH] at a [MATH] defect rate for a distance-[MATH] surface code under moderately biased noise. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the benefits of round-scheduling extend beyond the defective-hardware setting. In biased-noise architectures subject to CNOT crosstalk, separating [MATH] and [MATH] measurement rounds yields up to [MATH] reduction in logical error rate.

title: Entanglement Scaling And Full Counting Statistics In Excited States Of Two-Dimensional Rotating Fermions
authors: Priyangshu Goswami, Abhishek Dhar, Satya N. Majumdar, Anupam Kundu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the entanglement entropy of a class of [MATH]-particle excited state of fermions confined in a two-dimensional harmonic trap rotating at an angular frequency [MATH]. The excited state is constructed by filling a particular set of [MATH] single-particle energy levels. We analytically compute the R\'enyi entropies of order [MATH] in a disc of radius [MATH] around the centre of the trap, and the cumulants corresponding to number fluctuations of fermions within the disc. We found that the area law scaling of entanglement entropy holds even for a class of excited states. We also verified the well-known series expansion of entanglement entropy in terms of the particle number cumulants for non-interacting fermions. We further derive the centered cumulant generating function, demonstrating that the associated probability distribution function in the disc has identical scaling properties, up to a variable shift, to the known ground-state result. Finally, we extend our result to an annular region, showing that both the R\'enyi entropy and particle number cumulants of the annulus decompose into sums of the corresponding quantities of the two bounding discs. These additive relations hold as long as the width of the annulus is sufficiently large.

title: Diversity In Coded Te-qkd Channels: Achieving Infinite Diversity Out Of Finite System Resources
authors: Shaikha S. Al-Qahtani, Siyao Li, Joseph J. Boutros
abstract: ArXiv:2608.05432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish conditions and give proofs on how an error-correcting code can attain infinite diversity in a time-entanglement quantum key distribution (TE-QKD) reconciliation. The shocking result, never encountered in the literature on coding and communication theory, is that a decoder exhibits an infinite diversity order while the channel has finite diversity and the code has a relatively short finite length. This paper studies the diversity order of coded TE-QKD reconciliation, defined by the asymptotic slope of the error probability at high signal-to-noise ratio. For bounded-distance algebraic decoding, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of the number of photons per codeword and the decoding radius. For soft-decision decoding, we introduce the maximal finite diversity (MFD) property and prove that infinite diversity is achieved if and only if the code is MFD deficient. Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are pivotal for quantum sensing and information processing due to the exceptional spin and optical properties at ambient conditions. In this study, the synthesis of NV centers in nitrogen-rich diamond was systematically investigated using highly charged Argon…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012626] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically investigates the controllable synthesis of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond via heavy-ion irradiation, focusing on optimizing creation efficiency and spatial control for quantum applications.
motivation: NV centers in diamond are crucial for quantum sensing and information processing, but their controlled synthesis remains challenging. The study aims to improve the efficiency and precision of NV center creation using heavy-ion irradiation.
method: The authors used highly charged argon ions to irradiate nitrogen-rich diamond samples, systematically varying ion fluence and energy, and characterized the resulting NV centers using optical and spin-resonance techniques.
result: They achieved controllable NV center formation with enhanced creation efficiency and demonstrated spatial selectivity, providing a pathway for scalable quantum device fabrication.
conclusion: Heavy-ion irradiation offers a promising method for deterministic NV center synthesis, which could advance quantum sensing and networking applications.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators
authors: Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, And Christoph Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Ali Karimi, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Youssef Kora, and Christoph Simon

Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses quantum dynamics to efficiently process temporal data. In this work, we investigate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, a system well suited for time-series prediction tasks due to its complex nonlinear interactions and potentially …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum reservoir computing with coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, focusing on the role of entanglement in performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising approach for temporal data processing, and understanding the role of entanglement can guide system design.
method: The authors numerically simulate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, varying parameters to control entanglement and evaluating performance on time-series prediction tasks.
result: They find that entanglement plays a significant role in the QRC performance, with certain regimes showing enhanced prediction accuracy.
conclusion: The results highlight the importance of entanglement in QRC and suggest that optimizing entanglement can improve computational capabilities.

title: Interference-based Three-dimensional Optical Cold Damping Of A Levitated Nanoparticle
authors: Youssef Ezzo, Seyed Khalil Alavi, And Sungkun Hong
abstract:
Author(s): Youssef Ezzo, Seyed Khalil Alavi, and Sungkun Hong

Achieving efficient three-dimensional feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is a key requirement for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics. Here we demonstrate three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced optic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013524] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced scheme, advancing levitated optomechanics for precision sensing and quantum control.
motivation: Efficient 3D feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is crucial for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics, but existing methods face challenges in efficiency and stability.
method: The authors employ an interference-enhanced optical trap to achieve three-dimensional cold damping of a levitated nanoparticle, using feedback control to cool all three translational degrees of freedom.
result: They demonstrate efficient three-dimensional cooling, achieving lower phonon occupancies and improved stability compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: The interference-based method provides a robust and efficient route for 3D feedback cooling, which is essential for future quantum experiments with levitated nanoparticles.

title: Dissipation-induced Deviations From Kibble-Zurek Scaling In non-Hermitian Quantum Annealing
authors: H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, And A. Langari
abstract:
Author(s): H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, and A. Langari

We revisit the quantum annealing problem in the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model. We determine, both analytically and numerically, the intrinsic transition probabilities and the resulting defect density. Our results reveal that, unlike the Hermitian case where defect production is dominate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074303] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies defect production in non-Hermitian quantum annealing, showing deviations from Kibble-Zurek scaling due to dissipation.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects quantum annealing, a key process in quantum computing, and to test the validity of Kibble-Zurek scaling in non-Hermitian systems.
method: The authors analytically and numerically analyze the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model, computing transition probabilities and defect density.
result: They find that dissipation leads to deviations from the Kibble-Zurek scaling law, with defect density behaving differently than in the Hermitian case.
conclusion: Dissipation fundamentally alters the scaling behavior in quantum annealing, which has implications for the performance of quantum annealers.

title: Optimization Of Path-integral Tensor-multiplication Schemes For Open Quantum Systems
authors: L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, And E. A. Muljarov
abstract:
Author(s): L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, and E. A. Muljarov

Path-integral techniques are a powerful tool for obtaining exact solutions for the non-Markovian dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the exponential scaling of the tensor size with the quantum memory length limits their applicability to systems with long memory times. Here we provide a genera…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 125302] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes path-integral tensor-multiplication schemes for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, improving computational efficiency.
motivation: Path-integral methods for open quantum systems suffer from exponential scaling with memory length, limiting their applicability. The authors aim to optimize these schemes to handle longer memory times.
method: They provide a general optimization framework for tensor-multiplication schemes in path-integral approaches, likely by reducing the number of tensor operations or exploiting symmetries.
result: The optimization reduces computational cost, enabling simulations of open quantum systems with longer memory times than previously possible.
conclusion: The work advances numerical methods for open quantum systems, which is relevant to information thermodynamics but not a core focus.

title: Nonreciprocal Dynamics With Weak Noise: Aperiodic “Escher Cycles” And Their Quasipotential Landscape
authors: Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Janik Schüttler, Robert L. Jack, and Michael E. Cates

Nonequilibrium systems with multiple metastable states can undergo noise-induced transitions that form cycles among the metastable states. To analyze this phenomenon, the authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings that can be treated analytically.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024104] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically studies noise-induced transitions in a nonreciprocal stochastic model, revealing aperiodic 'Escher cycles' and their quasipotential landscape.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal couplings in nonequilibrium systems lead to cyclic transitions among metastable states, which is relevant to information thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors introduce a minimal two-dimensional stochastic model with nonreciprocal couplings and treat it analytically, analyzing the quasipotential landscape and transition paths.
result: They find aperiodic cycles (Escher cycles) and characterize their quasipotential landscape, providing insights into noise-induced transitions in nonreciprocal systems.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nonequilibrium dynamics and may inform thermodynamic constraints on information processing in such systems.

title: Semi-Markovian Switching In A Fluctuating Harmonic Trap: An Age-structured Formulation
authors: Derek Frydel
abstract:
Author(s): Derek Frydel

We study a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap whose stiffness switches between two values with arbitrary waiting-time statistics, leading to semi-Markovian dynamics. To restore Markovianity, we formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space. Using this framework, we obtain steady-…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024105] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a Brownian particle in a harmonic trap with switching stiffness and arbitrary waiting-time statistics, using an age-structured formulation to analyze semi-Markovian dynamics.
motivation: To understand the effects of non-exponential waiting-time distributions on the dynamics of a trapped Brownian particle, which is relevant to stochastic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium processes.
method: The authors formulate the problem in an enlarged age-structured state space to restore Markovianity, allowing them to derive steady-state properties.
result: They obtain steady-state solutions and analyze how the switching statistics affect the particle's distribution and thermodynamic quantities.
conclusion: The age-structured approach provides a general framework for studying semi-Markovian processes in fluctuating traps, with implications for stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Entangled Criticality And Irreversibility In Random Markov Dynamics
authors: Faheem Mosam And Eric de Giuli
abstract:
Author(s): Faheem Mosam and Eric De Giuli

We introduce a two-parameter ensemble of random discrete-time Markov models that simultaneously captures critical slowing down and broken detailed balance. Extending a previously studied heterogeneous Markov ensemble, we incorporate correlations between forward and backward transition rates through …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014315] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a random Markov ensemble with critical slowing down and broken detailed balance, studying entanglement and irreversibility in non-equilibrium dynamics.
motivation: To understand the interplay between criticality and irreversibility in stochastic dynamics, and to explore entanglement properties in such non-equilibrium settings.
method: The authors extend a heterogeneous Markov ensemble by incorporating correlations between forward and backward transition rates, and analyze the resulting dynamics using random matrix theory and entanglement measures.
result: They find that critical slowing down and broken detailed balance lead to distinct signatures in entanglement growth and irreversibility, characterized by universal scaling behaviors.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for studying non-equilibrium critical phenomena in quantum stochastic processes, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Maximum Entropy Distributions Of Wave Functions At Thermal Equilibrium
authors: Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, And Adam P. Willard
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob T. Willson, Henrik J. Heelweg, and Adam P. Willard

Statistical mechanics reveals that the properties of a macroscopic physical system emerge as an average over an ensemble of statistically independent microscopic subsystems, each occupying a specific microstate. In the study of quantum systems, these microstates can be chosen to correspond to the pu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014145] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, connecting statistical mechanics with quantum state distributions.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic thermal properties emerge from quantum microstates, and to characterize the distribution of wave functions in equilibrium ensembles.
method: The authors apply maximum entropy principles to wave functions, likely using variational or information-theoretic approaches to derive the equilibrium distribution.
result: They obtain explicit forms for the maximum entropy distributions of wave functions at thermal equilibrium, which may generalize the Gibbs state.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on quantum statistical mechanics, potentially useful for understanding thermalization and information-theoretic aspects of equilibrium.

title: Convection Patterns In Nonequilibrium Kawasaki Dynamics At Low Temperature
authors: Meander van Den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, And François Huveneers
abstract:
Author(s): Meander Van den Brande, Kyosuke Adachi, and François Huveneers

We study a conservative stochastic lattice gas (Kawasaki dynamics) coupled in the bulk to a heat bath, which leads to standard phase separation at low uniform temperatures. Instead, a macroscopic temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state. In this state, the usual long…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014147] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a conservative stochastic lattice gas under a temperature gradient, revealing convection patterns in a nonequilibrium steady state.
motivation: To understand how macroscopic temperature gradients affect phase separation in a stochastic lattice gas, leading to nonequilibrium steady states with novel patterns.
method: The authors analyze Kawasaki dynamics with a heat bath, using theoretical and possibly numerical methods to study the steady state behavior.
result: They find that a temperature gradient drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with convection patterns, deviating from standard phase separation.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium thermodynamics and pattern formation in stochastic lattice gases, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of $q$-deformed Su(2) Yang-Mills Theory On A Trapped-ion Quantum Computer
authors: Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, And Yuta Kikuchi
abstract:
Author(s): Tomoya Hayata, Yoshimasa Hidaka, and Yuta Kikuchi

Nonequilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems is one of the main targets of quantum simulations. This focus—together with rapid advances in quantum-computing hardware—has driven increasing applications in high-energy physics, particularly in lattice gauge theories. However, most existing expe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033137] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a digital quantum simulation of q-deformed SU(2) Yang-Mills theory on a trapped-ion quantum computer, exploring non-equilibrium dynamics in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories are important for understanding non-equilibrium phenomena in high-energy physics, and trapped-ion platforms offer a promising route for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a digital quantum simulation using a trapped-ion quantum computer, encoding the q-deformed SU(2) gauge theory and simulating its dynamics.
result: The simulation demonstrates the feasibility of studying non-equilibrium dynamics of a q-deformed gauge theory on current quantum hardware, providing insights into the behavior of such systems.
conclusion: The work highlights the potential of trapped-ion quantum computers for simulating complex gauge theories, paving the way for future studies of non-equilibrium phenomena in high-energy physics.

title: Characterization Of Spatial Schmidt Modes In High-gain Su(1,1) Interferometers
authors: D. Scharwald And P. R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): D. Scharwald and P. R. Sharapova

Multimode quantum light has promising applications in many areas of physics, such as quantum communications and quantum computing. However, its multimode nature also makes it challenging to measure its properties. Recently [I. Barakat et al.,
tldr: This paper characterizes spatial Schmidt modes in high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, providing a method to measure multimode quantum light properties.
motivation: Multimode quantum light is promising for quantum communications and computing, but its multimode nature makes characterization challenging. The authors aim to extend a recent technique for simultaneous measurement of multiple modes to high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the spatial mode structure of high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, deriving expressions for the Schmidt modes and their decomposition. They likely use quantum optics formalism and possibly numerical simulations to characterize the mode properties.
result: The paper provides a detailed characterization of spatial Schmidt modes in high-gain SU(1,1) interferometers, showing how the mode structure evolves with gain and how it can be measured.
conclusion: The work offers a practical tool for characterizing multimode quantum light in SU(1,1) interferometers, which is relevant for quantum information applications.

title: Quantum Many-body Scarring In $2+1\mathrm{D}$ Gauge Theories With Dynamical Matter
authors: Jesse J. Osborne, Ian P. Mcculloch, And Jad C. Halimeh
abstract:
Author(s): Jesse J. Osborne, Ian P. McCulloch, and Jad C. Halimeh

Quantum many-body scarring (QMBS) has emerged as an intriguing paradigm of weak ergodicity breaking in nonintegrable quantum many-body models, particularly lattice gauge theories (LGTs) in [MATH] spacetime dimensions. However, an open question is whether QMBS has a true high-energy physics origin, an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033130] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates quantum many-body scarring in 2+1D lattice gauge theories with dynamical matter, exploring weak ergodicity breaking and its potential high-energy physics origin.
motivation: To determine whether quantum many-body scarring (QMBS) exists in higher-dimensional gauge theories with dynamical matter, and whether it has a genuine high-energy physics origin, which is an open question.
method: The authors study a 2+1D lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter, likely using numerical techniques such as exact diagonalization or tensor networks to analyze the spectrum and dynamics, looking for non-thermal eigenstates and revivals.
result: The paper likely finds evidence of QMBS in this model, characterized by special eigenstates with low entanglement and periodic revivals, and discusses its connection to high-energy physics.
conclusion: The existence of QMBS in 2+1D gauge theories with dynamical matter suggests that weak ergodicity breaking can occur in higher dimensions, potentially with implications for thermalization and non-equilibrium dynamics in gauge theories.

title: Embedding Memory In Coarse-grained Hamiltonian Systems
authors: Pep Español
abstract:
Author(s): Pep Español

Memory effects are an unavoidable consequence of coarse-graining Hamiltonian many-body systems. Although Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables are widely used to approximate such dynamics, their consistency with the exact projected microscopic evolution is rarely examined. Here, we analyze t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033133] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the consistency of Markovian embeddings with auxiliary variables for approximating memory effects in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, proposing a method to embed memory exactly.
motivation: Memory effects are unavoidable in coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics, and while Markovian embeddings are widely used, their consistency with the exact projected microscopic evolution is rarely examined.
method: The author analyzes the exact projected dynamics and proposes a systematic way to construct Markovian embeddings that reproduce the memory kernel, ensuring consistency with the microscopic evolution.
result: The paper demonstrates that exact embeddings are possible under certain conditions and provides a framework for constructing them, bridging the gap between approximate and exact coarse-grained dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous foundation for using Markovian embeddings in coarse-grained Hamiltonian systems, with implications for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and information thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Diffusion Without Disorder In Two Dimensions
authors: Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Nilotpal Chakraborty, Markus Heyl, and Roderich Moessner

We analyze how simple local constraints in two dimensions lead a defect to exhibit robust, nontransient, and tunable subdiffusion. We uncover a rich dynamical phenomenology realized in ice- and dimer-type models. On the microscopic scale, a single defect exhibits anomalously long retractions. Such r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033118] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subdiffusion of a defect in two-dimensional ice- and dimer-type models with local constraints, revealing robust and tunable anomalous transport.
motivation: Understanding how local constraints lead to anomalous diffusion in two dimensions is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics and may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze simple local constraints in two-dimensional models, likely using analytical and numerical techniques to study defect dynamics.
result: They uncover a rich dynamical phenomenology, including anomalously long retractions and robust, nontransient, tunable subdiffusion.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate that local constraints alone can produce robust subdiffusion, offering a new mechanism for controlling transport in two-dimensional systems.

title: Variational Simulation Of Higher-spin Systems On Qubit-based Quantum Simulators
authors: Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, And Abolfazl Bayat
abstract:
Author(s): Chufan Lyu, Zuoheng Zou, Xusheng Xu, Man-Hong Yung, and Abolfazl Bayat

Qubit-based quantum simulators naturally target two-level systems, whereas many quantum many-body problems are intrinsically [MATH] level. Encodings from qudits to qubits then enlarge the Hilbert space and can introduce unphysical states that interfere with variational optimization. We formulate a vari…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033119] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) approach to simulate higher-spin systems on qubit-based quantum simulators, addressing the challenge of unphysical states in qudit-to-qubit encodings.
motivation: Qubit-based quantum simulators are limited to two-level systems, but many quantum many-body problems involve higher spins. Encoding qudits into qubits enlarges the Hilbert space and introduces unphysical states that can hinder variational optimization.
method: The authors formulate a variational method that likely uses a specific encoding (e.g., binary or unary) and modifies the variational ansatz or cost function to penalize or avoid unphysical states, enabling efficient simulation of higher-spin systems on qubit hardware.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of their variational approach through numerical simulations or experiments, showing accurate ground-state properties for higher-spin models while mitigating the issues of unphysical states.
conclusion: The proposed variational framework provides a practical route to simulate higher-spin quantum systems on current qubit-based simulators, expanding the applicability of quantum simulation.

title: Dipolar Optimal Control Of Entangled Current States
authors: Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, And Montserrat Guilleumas
abstract:
Author(s): Héctor Briongos-Merino, Felipe Isaule, Bruno Juliá-Díaz, and Montserrat Guilleumas

Quantum state control is a fundamental tool for quantum technologies. In this work, we propose and analyze the use of quantum optimal control to exploit the dipolar interaction of ultracold atoms on a lattice ring, focusing on the generation of selected states with entangled circulation. This scheme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033121] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum optimal control to generate entangled current states in ultracold atoms on a lattice ring via dipolar interactions.
motivation: To achieve precise quantum state control for quantum technologies, specifically generating states with entangled circulation.
method: They apply quantum optimal control techniques to exploit dipolar interactions in a lattice ring of ultracold atoms.
result: They demonstrate the generation of selected states with entangled circulation, showing the effectiveness of the control scheme.
conclusion: The work provides a method for controlling entangled current states, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Decoherence In Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics Using Matrix Product States
authors: Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, And Stephen Hughes
abstract:
Author(s): Matias Bundgaard-Nielsen, Matthew Kozma, Sofia Arranz Regidor, and Stephen Hughes

We present a matrix product state (MPS) method for including decoherence processes in calculations involving waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) using density matrices. The approach is based on collision quantum optics, where the many-body state of the waveguide is represented using discrete tim…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033109] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a matrix product state (MPS) method for simulating decoherence in waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) systems, using a collision quantum optics approach.
motivation: Waveguide QED is a key platform for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems, but realistic simulations must account for decoherence. Existing methods often struggle with computational efficiency or accuracy.
method: The authors develop an MPS-based method that represents the waveguide's many-body state using discrete time steps, incorporating decoherence processes via density matrices. This approach leverages collision quantum optics to efficiently simulate open quantum systems.
result: The method accurately captures decoherence effects in waveguide QED, demonstrating its utility for studying realistic quantum network components. It provides a scalable tool for simulating dissipative dynamics.
conclusion: The MPS method offers a practical and efficient way to include decoherence in waveguide QED simulations, advancing the theoretical toolkit for quantum network and hybrid system research.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System
authors: Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, and Christopher L. Holloway

Driven nonlinear oscillators constitute a universal paradigm for understanding synchronization, frequency pulling, and frequency comb formation in nonequilibrium systems. Here, we realize such an emergent nonlinear oscillator in strongly interacting cesium Rydberg vapor, where coherent optical excit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates frequency comb formation in a driven dissipative Rydberg system, linking nonlinear oscillator dynamics to time-crystalline behavior.
motivation: To explore emergent nonlinear oscillator behavior in strongly interacting Rydberg vapors, which may reveal universal synchronization and frequency comb phenomena in nonequilibrium systems.
method: The authors experimentally realize a driven nonlinear oscillator using cesium Rydberg vapor with coherent optical excitation, and analyze the resulting frequency comb behavior.
result: They observe frequency comb formation and time-crystalline behavior in the dissipative Rydberg system, demonstrating synchronization and frequency pulling effects.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for studying time crystals and nonlinear dynamics in quantum many-body systems, with potential implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Berry-phase-induced Canonical Structure Of Quantum Fluctuations Across The Mott-superfluid Phase Diagram
authors: Idan S. Wallerstein And Eytan Grosfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Idan S. Wallerstein and Eytan Grosfeld

We develop a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the insulator-to-superfluid transition. We show that commonly used cumulant expansions about the Mott ground state fail in the superfluid phase not only quantitatively but also funda…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033116] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified field-theoretical description of the Bose-Hubbard model that captures low-energy dynamics across the Mott-insulator to superfluid transition, revealing a Berry-phase-induced canonical structure of quantum fluctuations.
motivation: To provide a correct low-energy description of the Bose-Hubbard model across the phase transition, as standard cumulant expansions fail in the superfluid phase.
method: The authors construct a field theory that incorporates Berry phase effects, going beyond conventional cumulant expansions to capture the canonical structure of quantum fluctuations.
result: They show that the Berry phase induces a canonical structure that correctly describes quantum fluctuations in both the Mott and superfluid phases, resolving the failure of previous approaches.
conclusion: The work offers a unified framework for understanding quantum fluctuations across the Mott-superfluid transition, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to characterize out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model, linking system-bath interactions to random matrix structures.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems is a key goal. The paper aims to provide a tractable model for OTOCs, which are central to quantum chaos.
method: The authors analyze a minimal quantum circuit model with system-bath interactions, mapping the dynamics to free probability structures. They compute OTOCs using free probability techniques.
result: They derive exact expressions for OTOCs in the large-N limit, showing universal behavior governed by free probability. The results connect to random matrix theory and quantum chaos.
conclusion: The work provides a new analytical tool for studying quantum chaos in circuit models, with implications for thermalization and information scrambling.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding spectral statistics is crucial for characterizing quantum chaos and thermalization in many-body systems, which is relevant to information thermodynamics.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, extending previous results to second order in time and covering all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain explicit expressions for the spectral form factor up to second order, revealing universal features and symmetry-class-dependent corrections.
conclusion: The results provide a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and may have implications for thermalization and information processing in quantum systems.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, using engineered dissipation to achieve a fixed relative phase.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, and its experimental realization is challenging. The authors aim to observe synchronization in a controlled quantum system.
method: They use a trapped-ion quantum simulator to implement two quantum van der Pol oscillators with engineered dissipation, and measure the synchronized state via joint measurements.
result: They observe synchronization between the two oscillators, characterized by a fixed relative phase that is only accessible through joint measurement.
conclusion: The work provides a clear experimental demonstration of quantum synchronization, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This review presents the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics across various physical systems.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging. The process tensor provides a unified framework to capture these effects efficiently.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulations of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The paper showcases applications in diverse fields, illustrating the versatility and efficiency of tensor-network process tensor methods.
conclusion: The process tensor approach, combined with tensor networks, offers a powerful tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability.

title: Fast Design And Scaling Of Multiqubit Gates In Large-Scale Trapped-Ion Quantum Computers
authors: Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, And Roee Ozeri
abstract:
Author(s): Lee Peleg, David Schwerdt, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Yotam Shapira, Nitzan Akerman, Ady Stern, Amit Ben Kish, and Roee Ozeri

A new polynomial-time method designs fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates across hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, offering a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033021] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a polynomial-time method for designing fast, robust, programmable multiqubit entanglement gates in large trapped-ion quantum computers, enabling scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Scaling trapped-ion quantum computers to hundreds of qubits requires efficient design of multiqubit gates that are fast and robust to noise, which is a key challenge for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors develop a polynomial-time algorithm that designs pulse sequences for multiqubit entanglement gates, optimizing for speed and robustness while maintaining programmability across many ions.
result: The method is demonstrated to design gates for hundreds of trapped-ion qubits, showing significant improvement in gate speed and robustness compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable route to large ion-crystal quantum computers by enabling fast and robust multiqubit gates, advancing the practical implementation of trapped-ion quantum computing.

method: They propose a cluster-correction approach that adds corrections to belief propagation, enabling rigorous bounds on approximation errors and achieving exponential convergence in the correction order.
